protocol_type: Channel-partitioned, controller-mastered command-driven DRAM protocol. Each of 16 independent channels has its own CK_t/CK_c and its own row (R) / column (C) command/address bus. Row commands (activate/precharge/refresh/MRS) on R; column commands (read/write) on C, decoded per 32-bit pseudo-channel. Data is double-data-rate on the 64-bit channel DQ bus, framed by differential WDQS (write) / RDQS (read).

command_encoding.transfer: Double data rate referenced to quarter-speed CK: each command uses one rising-edge and one falling-edge CA transfer.

field_legend.WRX: Write X (fill burst all-zero / all-one, no data transfer)
field_legend.WXSA / WXSB: Write X select (value to be written for the X-fill)

commands.name: Power-down entry
commands.notes: CA-bus power-down (PD); no CKE; lasts until CS next goes high.

commands.name: Read DQ Calibration
commands.notes: Returns a fixed DQ calibration pattern.

commands.name: Multi-purpose command
commands.notes: Carries OP[7:0]; used for ZQ calibration etc.

commands.name: Self-refresh entry
commands.notes: Enter self-refresh; PD/DSE select power-down vs deep-sleep.

commands.name: Refresh
commands.notes: REFab (AB) or REFpb (per-bank round-robin); RFM selects Refresh Management.

commands.name: Column Address Select
commands.notes: Carries WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR, WRX, WXSA/WXSB; prepares WCK sync — does NOT select a column.

commands.name: Read-32
commands.notes: Double-length (BL32) read; start position via C0/B3.

wck_synchronization.WS_FS: Free-Start — start WCK immediately; may precede multiple reads/writes (multiple banks).
wck_synchronization.WS_RD: Read-optimized — optimize WCK timing for an immediately following read.
wck_synchronization.WS_WR: Write-optimized — optimize WCK timing for an immediately following write.
wck_synchronization.rule: The CAS command carries WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR to lock internal WCK to CK before the high-speed transfer. Unlike LPDDR4, the CAS command in LPDDR5 comes BEFORE the read/write and primarily serves this synchronization role (it does not select a column).

channels.name: CK_t, CK_c
channels.description: Per-channel differential clock; commands registered at rising edges; channels need not be synchronous.

channels.name: C[ ] (column command/address)
channels.description: READ/WRITE with column address; decoded independently per 32-bit pseudo-channel.

channels.name: DQ
channels.description: 64-bit-per-channel data bus (1024 bits/stack); double data rate.

channels.name: ECC / parity bits
channels.description: Link-ECC and DQ-parity protecting data and command/address.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: No per-beat handshake; each command is committed at the rising edge of CK_t/CK_c on its channel; data follows at deterministic latency.
READ data appears at read latency from READ, framed by DRAM-driven RDQS.
WRITE data is launched framed by WDQS at write latency from WRITE.
Row (R) and column (C) commands can be issued in parallel within a channel.
Column commands decode independently for each of the two 32-bit pseudo-channels.
Channels are independent; no cross-channel interlock.

frame_format.row_command_frame: Command on R[ ] across one or more CK cycles; ACTIVATE/PRECHARGE/REFRESH/RFM/MRS with bank-group/bank/row.
frame_format.column_command_frame: Command on C[ ] encoding READ/WRITE with column; decoded per 32-bit pseudo-channel.
frame_format.data_frame: Burst on the 64-bit DQ bus (32 bits/pseudo-channel), double-data-rate, framed by WDQS (write)/RDQS (read).

comparison_to_lpddr4: LPDDR4 column names C0-C9 are renamed in LPDDR5 to B0-B3 and C0-C5; writes start at a multiple-of-16 address (B0-B3 zero); reads may use a non-zero B3.
LPDDR5 widens the CA bus to 7 bits at double data rate, so commands arrive at the same cadence as LPDDR4 despite the quarter-speed CK.
In LPDDR5 the CAS command precedes the read/write and synchronizes WCK (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR); in LPDDR4 the CAS-2 command followed the column command.
LPDDR5 provides one set of full-speed WCK clocks per byte (vs per 16 bits in LPDDR4).

commands.description: Open a row in the selected bank-group/bank.
Close the open row and restore bitlines.
Burst read; decoded per pseudo-channel; DRAM drives DQ + RDQS.
Burst write; decoded per pseudo-channel; controller drives DQ + WDQS.
Program a mode register with the channel idle.
DRAM self-refreshes; clock may stop; exit re-synchronizes.

pseudo_channel_rules: Each 64-bit channel splits into two 32-bit pseudo-channels.
Pseudo-channels share the channel's clock and the row-side command/address bus.
Pseudo-channel mode improves access granularity and bus efficiency.
command_bus: CA[9:0] double-data-rate command/address bus per channel; each command is presented over two CK edges and captured on CK_t/CK_c. CABI_n may invert the CA word to cap driven-low lines.

commands.name: ACTIVATE
commands.desc: Open a row in a bank (row address on CA).

commands.name: PRECHARGE
commands.desc: Close a row in a bank / all banks.

commands.name: READ
commands.desc: Column read, BL16; data returned on DQ clocked by WCK; read CRC on EDC.

commands.name: WRITE
commands.desc: Column write, BL16; data on DQ clocked by WCK; write CRC checked on EDC.

commands.name: MODE REGISTER SET
commands.desc: Load a value into a mode register MR0..MR15.

commands.name: SELF REFRESH ENTRY/EXIT
commands.desc: Enter/exit self refresh (and hibernate self refresh).

addressing: Row/column addressing within bank groups and banks (e.g. 4 bank groups x 4 banks = 16 banks per channel, density dependent). Column accesses move BL16 per DQ.
